title: CheckYourVibe configuration
description: Top-level configuration for a checkyourvibe-checked repository.

$schema.description: JSON Schema location for editor autocompletion and validation.

packs.description: Rule packs to enable. Every rule in a listed pack is enabled unless it is disabled in `rules`.

analyzers.description: Analyzers to load. Each entry declares how the core reaches a language-specific analyzer.

rules.description: Per-rule overrides. A rule set to `false` is disabled; a rule object carries an optional `severity` plus rule-specific options.

overrides.description: Per-path rule overrides, applied in array order after the base `rules`. A later override wins over an earlier one for the same rule id. Use this so one directory (e.g. a CLI) can carry a different rule posture than the rest of the repository, without disabling a rule globally.

suppressions.description: Individual violations deferred rather than fixed. Every suppression requires a reason AND an expiry: a bare ignore directive is deliberately unsupported, because this project's own rule guidance argues against exactly that pattern. An expired suppression stops suppressing and is named in the run output.

strict.description: When `true`, skipped files and other non-fatal conditions cause a non-zero exit.

exclude.description: Globs excluded on top of each analyzer's own `exclude` list.

executorConfig.description: The executor lanes this repository dispatches work to (spec 0011). Omitting this key is a supported state: with no lane declared, the localhost view shows each lane's running count and whatever cap the dispatch log itself recorded, and says a declared cap is not on hand rather than inventing one.

lanes.description: Every lane the core may consider. A lane is declared here and never discovered: nothing the core can read reports which executors are installed, how many dispatches an account tolerates, or what models a vendor currently ships.

meteredLanesEnabled.description: Ids of metered lanes this repository has opted into, named one by one. A lane declared with `billing.kind` of `metered` is rejected unless its id appears here, so a metered lane cannot arrive by copying a lane block; and an id here that names no declared metered lane is rejected too. The core still never selects a metered lane on its own — reaching one also requires a dispatch that names it (spec 0011 Requirements 1.3, 1.5).

stallAfterMinutes.description: Minutes without a newly opened dispatch, while open work exists and a lane is free, before the run is reported as stalled. Omitted, it is 30. This number is how long silence goes on before a reader is told about it, and nothing more: a stall names the idle lanes and no cause, and no subscription's reset window informed the default, because the core has no reading of any account's limit (spec 0036 Requirement 4; spec 0011 Requirement 7.5).

maxConcurrentDispatches.description: The most dispatches that may be open across every lane at once (spec 0041 Requirement 3.1). Omitted, it resolves to the sum of the caps of the lanes that accept dispatched work, which by construction never binds before those caps do — so the default adds no limit, and declaring another lane raises the ceiling without a second number to maintain. Set it lower to hold a run below what the lanes would otherwise permit. A dispatch refused by this reports `at-global-cap`, which is deliberately a different state from a single lane being at its own cap.

laneDeclaration.description: One executor lane: what backs it, how much of it the core may use at once, how it is paid for, and which models it offers per task kind.

id.description: Names this lane in the dispatch log, in every scheduling refusal, and in the localhost view. A dispatch that reaches a metered lane names this id.

agentId.description: The `agents` entry backing this lane — which CLI is invoked and how it authenticates. Declaring a lane here is separate consent from listing that agent in `agents`: an agent configured for hooks, instructions, guidance or MCP does not become an executor by being listed there (spec 0011 Requirement 5.2).

concurrencyCap.description: The most dispatches the core will run against this lane at once. A self-imposed number the user tunes, NOT a reading of the vendor's rate limit: an authenticated CLI reports no remaining quota, so nothing here is measured from the account. Reaching this cap means this configured number is in use, and says nothing about the account's real limit (spec 0011 Requirements 3.1, 7.1, 7.2).

orchestrator.description: True for the lane that is the agent session issuing dispatches. It is named like any other lane wherever a dispatch is shown, and is subject to the same cap, cooldown and escalation rules (spec 0011 Requirements 6.1, 6.2). At most one lane may set this.

acceptsDispatch.description: Whether the lane may receive an ordinary dispatched task. The orchestrating lane is brought into the run by the session issuing dispatches, so its capacity is reserved for planning, review and integration unless the author says otherwise: when this is absent and `orchestrator` is `true` the resolved value is `false`, otherwise `true`. The one exception is a repository declaring exactly one lane, where reserving it would leave every dispatch refused with no alternative to name, so a sole orchestrating lane resolves to `true` (spec 0041 Requirement 2.2). The default is applied by `configuredLanes`, not by the schema, because it depends on `orchestrator` and on how many lanes are declared.

executes.description: How work reaches this lane. `cli` spawns the agent's own program, which is every lane's normal case. `subagent` means the orchestrating session runs the task itself, as a sub-agent of its own, and the core judges the result by observed effect exactly as it judges a CLI's (spec 0041 Requirement 2.1). Absent, this resolves to `subagent` for a sole orchestrating lane and `cli` for every other. Like `acceptsDispatch`, the default is applied by `configuredLanes` because it depends on how many lanes are declared.

models.description: Which models this lane offers for each task kind. A lane that declares no ordering for a dispatch's task kind is not a candidate for that dispatch (spec 0011 Requirement 8.4).

laneBilling.description: How this lane is paid for.

kind.description: `subscription` is a flat-rate plan the user already holds, invoked as an authenticated CLI. `metered` is billed per token or per request: it must additionally be named in `executor.meteredLanesEnabled`, it is labelled as billed at every point it is shown to the user, and it is reachable only by a dispatch that names it (spec 0011 Requirements 1.2 - 1.5).

permitsBilledOverage.description: Whether the user has configured this lane as permitting billed overage past its included capacity. A configuration fact the user supplied, not a reading of their account: the core reports no dollar figure and no token count for a dispatch (spec 0011 Requirements 9.6, 9.7).

laneModelOffering.description: The models this lane offers for one task kind.

kind.description: The kind of work a dispatch declares: `mechanical-transformation` is work whose finished state a gate can check completely, `judgment-required` is work the gates cannot fully verify. It describes the work, not a model (spec 0011 Requirement 8.1).

ordering.description: This lane's own models for the kind, strongest first, as the person who maintains this lane judges its vendor's lineup. The core treats the list as opaque: it requests the last entry — the weakest — for every dispatch, and steps one position up only after an observed gate failure. It does not re-rank the list, merge it with another lane's, or compare a position in it against a position in another lane's (spec 0011 Requirements 8.2, 8.3, 9.1, 9.3).

id.description: Short identifier used in error messages and routing.

package.description: Node module specifier or relative path to an analyzer manifest.

configOverride.description: A per-path rule override: `rules`-shaped settings that apply only to files matching one of `files`.

files.description: Non-empty list of globs, matched against each file's repo-relative path with forward slashes.

reason.description: Why this path gets different treatment. Required and non-empty — an override without a stated reason is a blanket exemption, which this feature exists to avoid.

rules.description: Per-rule overrides for the matching files. Same shape as the top-level `rules`: a rule set to `false` is disabled; a rule object carries an optional `severity` plus rule-specific options.

ruleOverride.description: Per-rule setting: an object overrides severity and rule options; `false` disables the rule.

oneOf.description: Rule-specific override. Any properties beyond `severity` are passed to the rule as options.

severity.description: Overridden severity. When omitted the rule manifest's default severity is used.

ruleId.description: The rule being suppressed. An unknown rule id is a configuration error — usually a rename nobody propagated.

target.description: Glob matched against a violation's repository-relative path. With `fingerprint`, this is instead the exact repository-relative path of the file holding the pinned finding — the `path` of its entry in checkyourvibe.baseline.json — and glob syntax is rejected.

reason.description: Why this is being deferred rather than fixed. Required: an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from an oversight six months later.

expires.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which this stops suppressing. Required, so a deferral cannot become permanent by inattention.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the normalized offending snippet, copied from the finding's entry in checkyourvibe.baseline.json. Present together with `occurrence`, it pins the suppression to one finding — the same durable identity the baseline uses — so a violation added to the same file later is still reported.

occurrence.description: Index among the findings sharing this file, rule and fingerprint, copied from the same baseline entry. Required alongside `fingerprint`: many rules report the same short snippet throughout a file, so a fingerprint on its own would defer all of them.
